chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'From the happiness of the Muslim person is the spacious dwelling.'
ai.seo_question: What is considered a sign of happiness for a Muslim according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi is often interpreted not merely as a material preference but as a practical necessity for maintaining privacy (haya) and facilitating worship, which are central to spiritual well-being. The chain of narration through Al-Sakuni highlights the transmission of this value from the Imams, linking domestic comfort directly to the concept of sa'adah (happiness/blessing). This perspective underscores that adequate living space is a means to achieve tranquility (sakinah), thereby supporting the holistic Islamic ideal of a balanced life.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘From happiness of the Muslim person is the spacious dwelling’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Of the good fortune for a Muslim man is spaciousness of the house.’”
